consensus.title: Incorrect full‑buffer check leads to silent overwrites
Off-by-one in ring buffer overflow check

responses.content:
* [WARNING] [BOUNDS] Zero-capacity ring buffer crashes on push (RingBuffer.__init__/push)
  - Issue: `RingBuffer(0)` creates an empty buffer, but `push()` then evaluates modulo by `len(self._buf)`, raising `ZeroDivisionError`. Negative capacities similarly produce an empty list and fail on the first push instead of rejecting invalid configuration.
  - Fix: Validate `capacity <= 0` in `__init__` and raise `ValueError` before initializing the buffer.

* [CRITICAL] [LOGIC] Off-by-one in ring buffer overflow check (push, line 7)
    - Issue: The guard `self._count > len(self._buf)` allows exactly one extra `push` beyond capacity before raising `BufferFull`. When `_count == len(self._buf)` (buffer is full), the condition is false, so the write proceeds and `_count` becomes `capacity + 1`. The invariant that `_count` tracks valid items is broken: subsequent reads indexed by `_count` or by offset from `_head` will return stale/overwritten data or index out of range. A caller that catches `BufferFull` and assumes the buffer is now full will observe silent data corruption.
    - Fix: Change the comparison to `>=`:
      ```python
      if self._count >= len(self._buf):
          raise BufferFull()
      ```

* [CRITICAL] LOGIC Incorrect full‑buffer check leads to silent overwrites (at push method)
  - Issue: The push method uses `if self._count > len(self._buf):` to detect a full buffer. When the buffer is exactly full (`_count == capacity`), the condition is false, so the method overwrites the oldest element instead of raising `BufferFull`. This causes silent data loss/corruption once the buffer reaches capacity.
  - Fix: Change the check to `if self._count >= len(self._buf):` (or `==`) and raise `BufferFull` before writing, e.g.:
        if self._count == len(self._buf):
            raise BufferFull
        self._buf[self._head] = item
        self._head = (self._head + 1) % len(self._buf)
        self._count += 1

* [CRITICAL] [BOUNDS] Off‑by‑one buffer full detection (at push)
  - Issue: The condition `if self._count > len(self._buf):` permits the buffer to accept one more item than its allocated capacity. After `capacity` pushes, `_count` equals `capacity`. The next push passes the check, writes into the next slot, increments `_head` (wrapping), and increments `_count` to `capacity+1`. This violates the ring‑buffer invariant that `_count` must never exceed `len(self._buf)`, leading to silent overwrites and loss of the oldest element.
  - Fix: Change the guard to `if self._count >= len(self._buf): raise BufferFull`. This ensures the buffer raises before storing an item when it is truly full, preserving the capacity bound.
